s1.syndrome_frame: Acute abdominal pain with peritonism and sepsis, complicated by respiratory failure
salient_findings: Multi-station mediastinal lymphadenopathy and pulmonary consolidation
key_facts: 60-year-old man with history of heavy cigarette smoking
History of emphysema, hypertension, and prostate cancer in remission
Presented with 4-hour history of acute right lower-quadrant abdominal pain
Fever (38.5°C), hypotension (systolic blood pressure 90 mmHg), and tachycardia (heart rate 110/min) on admission
Peritonism in the right lower quadrant on examination
Contrast-enhanced CT showed perforated appendix with collection and surrounding fat stranding
Innumerable hepatic nodules, mural thickening of the cecum and sigmoid colon, and lymphadenopathy on CT
Pulmonary consolidation and collapse in the right lower lobe on CT
Underwent exploratory laparotomy with subtotal colectomy and end ileostomy
Remained ventilated postoperatively
Failed extubation attempt on day 3
Died on day 6 after withdrawal of care

shortlist.label: Colorectal adenocarcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Mural thickening of the cecum and sigmoid colon, lymphadenopathy, and hepatic nodules on CT suggest metastatic disease

shortlist.label: Small cell lung carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: History of heavy cigarette smoking, bulky mediastinal lymphadenopathy, and pulmonary consolidation on CT

shortlist.label: Perforated appendicitis
shortlist.why_kept: Acute right lower-quadrant abdominal pain, peritonism, and CT findings of a perforated appendix

shortlist.label: Sepsis
shortlist.why_kept: Fever, hypotension, and tachycardia on admission, with evidence of peritonism and organ dysfunction

shortlist.label: Metastatic disease from prostate cancer
shortlist.why_kept: History of prostate cancer in remission, with multiple hepatic nodules and lymphadenopathy on CT

raw.rationale: The patient's CT scan showed mural thickening of the cecum and sigmoid colon, and the exploratory laparotomy revealed a thickened, woody sigmoid colon, which are indicative of a primary colorectal malignancy. The presence of innumerable hepatic nodules and lymphadenopathy also suggests metastatic disease, which is consistent with advanced colorectal cancer.

rejected.label: Small cell lung carcinoma
rejected.why: While the patient has a history of heavy cigarette smoking, which is a risk factor for lung cancer, the primary findings of mural thickening of the cecum and sigmoid colon and the presence of a thickened, woody sigmoid colon point more towards a primary colorectal malignancy.

rejected.label: Perforated appendicitis
rejected.why: Although the patient did have a perforated appendix, this is likely a secondary finding and not the primary diagnosis, as the patient had more extensive disease involving the colon and liver.

rejected.label: Sepsis
rejected.why: Sepsis is a likely complication of the patient's condition, given the perforated appendix and peritonism, but it is not the underlying diagnosis that explains the patient's overall clinical presentation.

rejected.label: Metastatic disease from prostate cancer
rejected.why: The patient's prostate cancer is in remission, and the findings on CT and laparotomy are more consistent with a primary colorectal malignancy rather than metastatic prostate cancer.
